stem.text: Which statement explains why calcium has a higher melting point than barium?

A.text: Calcium cations are smaller than barium cations and have a stronger attraction to the delocalised electrons.

B.text: The structure of calcium is partly giant molecular.

C.text: There are more delocalised electrons in calcium than in barium as it has a lower ionisation energy.

D.text: There is greater repulsion between barium atoms as they have more complete electron shells than calcium atoms.
